message.content:
**Freezing point of water at 10 kPa**

At a pressure of 10 kPa (≈ 0.099 atm) the melting/freezing point of ice is **about –1 °C**.  
This value comes from the water‑ice phase diagram: the melting temperature drops roughly 0.01 °C for every 1 kPa decrease in pressure above the triple‑point pressure (≈ 0.006 atm).  

| Pressure | Freezing point (approx.) |
|----------|--------------------------|
| 101.3 kPa (1 atm) | 0 °C |
| 10 kPa | –1 °C |
| 1 kPa | –2 °C |
| 0.006 atm (triple point) | 0 °C |

So, at 10 kPa the water will freeze at roughly **–1 °C**.
